# dsh-hide-account-models

A DeepSeek Harness bundle that
hides the signed-in DeepSeek account model group from the model picke

r and keeps
every dispatch on the official API-key provider.
| In the picker | After enabling |

| DeepSeek account models (signed-in quota) | hidden |
| `deepseek-official` models (API key) | kept
, and the only selectable group |

The plugin has no settings page and no client half. Turn it on or off from
**Plugins**, exactly like

settings page and no client half. Turn it on or off from
**Plugins**, exactly like any other bundle.
## Why

Signing in to the desktop app adds a `deepseek-account` provider next to the
`deepseek-official` API

-key provider. Both appear in the composer menu. If a
conversation keeps an account model selected,

its next request can spend on the
account even when you intended to use your API key.

This bundle removes the account group from the catalog the picker is built from,
and rewrites an alr

eady-saved account selection to `deepseek-official` before the
request leaves the Host.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0` (declared in `engines.dsh`).
- An **official API key config

ured** under **Settings → Models** (`deepseek-official`).
Without it there is no model left to selec

t after the account group is hidden.
Configure the key first, then enable this plugin.
- Any operati
ng system. The plugin is platform-neutral.
## Install

Replace `desktop` with the profile you actually start. GitHub installs need Git
on the machine, beca
use DSH asks the repository before downloading.
### From GitHub (recommended, pinned to a tag)
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### From the Release tarball (no Git needed)
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### From the Plugins page

Open **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste the repository address or the tarball URL,
and restart DSH if t

he page asks. Installing by bare package name only works for
a package published to npm; this bundle
is currently distributed from GitHub.

After a restart, `deepseek-account` is gone from the model menu. Nothing else
changes: no new page,
no new toolbar item.
## How it works
Three seams, all in the Host process:

1. **The catalog.** Both browser model surfaces build their catalog from
`ctx.llm.listProviders()`.

The plugin wraps that method and drops the
`deepseek-account` entry, so the account group disappears

from the menu, the
search index, and keyboard navigation at the same time.
2. **Prepared calls.** A

conversation that already saved an account model would
still have it in the Host's per-session sele

ction cache. The plugin wraps
`llm.prepareCall()` (the Agent loop and title generation) and rewrites

only
`provider: "deepseek-account"` to `deepseek-official`. Every other field,
including the model

id, is preserved.
3. **Direct streams.** Some callers dispatch through `llm.stream()` without
prepar

ing first — the default compaction summarizer is one. The same
provider rewrite is applied there.

The plugin intentionally does not listen to `agent/request`: that hook is
deprecated in DSH 0.2.x, a

nd the Agent loop rejects a provider or model change
there before dispatch. Rewriting at `prepareCal

l`/`stream` is the supported
place to keep the route on the API key.

Disabling or removing the plugin restores the original methods and announces the
change, so the acco
unt group comes back immediately without a restart.
## Before you enable it

- **Configure `deepseek-official` first.** The plugin does not check whether the
official route has

a usable key. If it does not, the picker will be empty and
requests will fail with the official rout

e's error instead of spending on the
account. That failure is intentional; it is safer than a silent

fallback.
- **Old conversations.** A session saved with an account model shows the
"select a model"

prompt until you choose an official model. If you send before
choosing, the request is prepared aga

inst `deepseek-official` with the same
model id.
- **Model ids are not translated.** If the account

catalog and the official
catalog name a model differently, a rewritten request can be rejected by th

e
provider. Pick an official model in that conversation once and the problem
does not come back.
- *

*Nothing is rewritten on disk.** Session logs keep their history; only the
outgoing request is rerou

hing is rewritten on disk.** Session logs keep their history; only the
outgoing request is rerouted.
## Privacy
The plugin is a pure in-process filter:

- **No network requests.** It never contacts DeepSeek or any other host.
- **No files.** It does not

read or write configuration, credentials, logs, or
session data.
- **No telemetry.** It reports not
it never resolves, reads, or copies an API key or account token.

It reads provider metadata (`id`, `name`) from the `llm` service and writes only
one thing: the in-m
emory provider list that the UI reads.
## Enable, disable, remove

Turn the bundle off with its switch in **Plugins**; the account group returns at
once. Remove it ent

ndle off with its switch in **Plugins**; the account group returns at
once. Remove it entirely with:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Removing the plugin does the same; it has no state to clean up.
## Compatibility

- DSH `0.2.2-rc.1` through `0.2.x`. The bundle relies on the provider ids
`deepseek-account` / `deep

seek-official` and on `ctx.llm.listProviders()` and
`ctx.llm.prepareCall()` from that release line.

- A future DSH release that renames those providers or stops projecting the
provider list into the c

atalog will make the filter a no-op. Disable the
bundle if the picker misbehaves rather than leaving

it installed.
- This is a community plugin, not an official DeepSeek project.
## Development
Pure ESM JavaScript, zero dependencies, no build step. Run the unit tests:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The tests use a fake `llm` service and a fake Cordis context. They cover the
provider filter, the `p

repareCall` and `stream` rewrites, restoration of the
prototype methods through a traceable proxy, a

nd coexistence with another plugin
that patches the same method later.
